name: BlackRock
description: BlackRock is the world's largest asset manager, with $14.0 trillion of client assets at Dec 31, 2025. Most revenue is a small annual percentage fee on money it manages, from its iShares ETFs ($5.5 trillion), index funds and active funds, and increasingly from private-market funds after buying Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) and HPS. It also sells Aladdin, the risk and portfolio software many large investors run their books on, plus Preqin data, for subscription and technology fees ($2.0B in 2025). About 79% of 2025 revenue was base advisory fees and securities lending, 6% performance fees, 8% technology and subscriptions, and 6% distribution fees.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge, not re-checked. SEC SIC code is 6211. The 10-K states BlackRock does not engage in proprietary trading; it acts as a fiduciary.

hq.note: From general knowledge; cover page not re-read in this pass.

businessLines.name: Investment advisory, administration and securities lending (base fees)
businessLines.how: A recurring percentage-of-assets fee, low on index ETFs and higher on active and private-market funds, so revenue rises with markets and net inflows; securities lending adds a share of fees from lending client-owned securities.
businessLines.description: Fees on assets under management across equity, fixed income, multi-asset, alternatives, index and cash.

businessLines.name: Technology services and subscription (Aladdin, eFront, Preqin, Cachematrix)
businessLines.how: Multi-year software and data contracts paid annually by investment firms, based on assets or number of users; recurring and not directly tied to market levels.

businessLines.name: Investment advisory performance fees
businessLines.how: A share of investment gains above a hurdle on alternative and some other funds; lumpy.

businessLines.name: Distribution fees
businessLines.how: Fees on certain funds sold through intermediaries, most of which is passed on to the distributors.

brands.name: iShares
brands.share: $5.47T AUM Dec 31, 2025; the 10-K calls BlackRock the leading ETF provider in the world

brands.name: Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP)
brands.note: Acquired; closed around October 1, 2024 per filing tags

brands.name: HPS Investment Partners
brands.note: Acquisition appears in the FY2025 10-K; closing date not extracted
